newsitem.title: POLAND: New highs seen on Warsaw bourse, correction later.
newsitem.headline: New highs seen on Warsaw bourse, correction later.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange hit four consecutive 33-month highs this week in heavy turnovers and analysts saw new records early next week but said a profit-taking correction was likely later.

They said that after gaining 25 percent since mid-December and jumping to levels unseen since March 1994, investors would be tempted to take profits. But analysts expected the 16,000 point level to offer a strong support.
"I don't think there will be a trend reversal, but there surely will be a correction, perhaps late next week or later," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
The main all-share WIG index rose 4.1 percent to 16,628.1 points since last Friday close.
Analysts said the stocks, trading at 16.2 times historic earnings, seemed fairly valued.

But they believed the bourse was in an uptrend fuelled by foreign buying as international investors, encouraged by the worldwide bullish mood, saw Poland's overall growth potential leaving the bourse some more room for growth.

They said the growth driven mainly by demand for large-cap stocks, was unlikely to be affected by a spate of late January and early February initial offers of smaller firms worth a total of about 200 million zlotys.

On Monday electric gauge maker Apator SA starts its 1.4- million-share offering, chemical company Viscoplast SA opens subscription of 900,000 shares and construction company Unibud SA is offering one million shares.
Carpet maker Lentex SA starts its 1.4-million-share initial public offering on Tuesday.

Analysts said Friday's figure of food prices growth in the second 10 days in January was unlikely to move the market in either direction after the central bank said it had postponed any decisions on interest rates until February.
Analysts said current growth was likely to be slowed by phases of stabilisations and profit-taking, before it is hit by a deeper slide.

But they saw only forthcoming parliamentary elections due in the last quarter and large privatisations due around mid-year significantly cooling investor sentiment later in the year. Analysts said Optimus outperformed the market, rising 31.3 percent this week, after it showed good December and 1996 earnings, but they could not explain Universal 21.2-percent surge.
